questions: Q1: What CLI interface should hlx inspect netsuite expose?
Q2: What CLI interface should hlx run expose?
Q3: Should the CLI expose an --env flag for either command?
Q4: What basePath should hlx run use — the default /api/inspect or an override?
Q5: Does either command need NetSuite-specific error handling in the CLI?

answers.answer: hlx inspect netsuite should support two modes via body type discriminator: (a) SuiteQL queries matching the db subcommand interface exactly: --repo <name> --query '<SuiteQL>' (recommended), --query-file <path> (for complex queries), and positional query argument (convenience); (b) Script log retrieval with flags: --repo <name> --logs --script-id <id> [--date-from <date>] [--date-to <date>] [--log-type <type>]. The --logs flag discriminates between query and log modes. Default mode (no --logs flag) is SuiteQL query.

answers.answer: hlx run is a new top-level command (not under inspect) following the configOrHelp pattern from src/index.ts:26-35. Interface: hlx run --repo <name> '<code>' (inline), hlx run --repo <name> --script-file <path> (from file), optional --modules <comma-separated> for specifying NetSuite modules. The handler follows the same resolveRepo -> hxFetch -> console.log pattern. New module at src/run/index.ts with a new case in src/index.ts switch.

answers.answer: No. The environment (PRODUCTION vs SANDBOX) is determined server-side from the inspection token's nsEnv claim (set by configureInspectionForStep in the orchestrator). Exposing an --env flag would be misleading and insecure — the server ignores client-specified environments. The agent doesn't need to know which environment it's querying. A human-facing --env flag is a future consideration (product/product.md Future Considerations).

answers.answer: hlx run uses the default basePath '/api/inspect' because the server endpoint is POST /api/inspect/:repositoryId/run (under the inspect prefix, per helix-global-server AD-1). No basePath override needed. The hxFetch call is: hxFetch(config, '/${repoId}/run', { method: 'POST', body: { code, modules? } }).

answers.answer: No. The existing hxFetch() error handling (http.ts) covers 429 (rate limit with Retry-After), 401 (unauthorized), and 5xx (server errors) with 3-attempt retry and exponential backoff. The server translates NetSuite-specific errors into standard HTTP errors with descriptive messages (via translateNsError in ns-gm-credential-test-service.ts:108-127). The CLI displays the error message from the server response. No NetSuite-specific error handling needed in the CLI.

statement: helix-cli needs two additions: (1) hlx inspect netsuite — new case in inspect router + new handler file (src/inspect/netsuite.ts) following the db.ts template for SuiteQL queries and a --logs mode for script log retrieval, and (2) hlx run — new top-level case in main dispatcher + new module (src/run/index.ts) for arbitrary SuiteScript execution. Both use the default basePath '/api/inspect' because the server routes both surfaces under the inspect prefix. Both use existing hxFetch with dual-mode auth and retry. No --env flag (token-bounded). No NetSuite-specific error handling. Zero new dependencies. The implementation is a direct application of established patterns with minimal risk.
